# Frozen legacy cache fixtures

These are synthetic Linux x86_64 bincode 1.3.3 (`bincode::options()`) bytes generated from the ordered wire declarations at `bd62b8c4e07269e5314fac06c6d23262dc714633`. They are not produced with the current `UnifiedMessage`, so adding a field cannot silently update the expected layout.

The directory's `.gitattributes` keeps JSONL sources LF-terminated and binary payloads unchanged on every checkout, including Windows, because frozen cache states retain exact source byte offsets and prefix hashes.

Generic envelopes v4–v10 use their released message layouts. MiCode v8–v11 use the corresponding v7–v10 entry inside `Vec<(Entry, Option<Vec<MiMoRowMetadata>>)>`. Every entry contains estimated $7.25, authoritative $0 and authoritative $0.375 fictional rows. Token buckets, fractional row timestamp bits, parent linkage and retention markers verify field alignment. Optional incremental-state slots are `None`; existing cache unit tests cover populated incremental states.

Fixtures contain no real user data or credentials. The loader test reads each original without modifying it, rewrites to the current format, then reads the new file warm and compares messages and MiCode provenance.

`codex-v10-parser15.bin` was exported by the unmodified cache writer and native `CachedSourceEntry` / `CodexParseState` types at upstream `6abf7213c383c527ee8e697c445f230708cd7249`, with only a synthetic export test added. It has populated incremental state (ordinal 129, provider gateway, pending turn and turn coverage), so the migration test cannot pass merely by serializing the current layout. Its source path is synthetic.

`codex-v10-parser14.bin` comes from the parent of that upstream merge, using the same original writer and synthetic values but no ordinal field. It verifies rejection by parser version before payload decoding and preservation of the old bytes.

`codex-v10-parser18.bin` was exported by the unmodified parser, native cache types and original writer at upstream `3f4559e00a947bc27605ee7419d3bcc6eac8ff50`. SHA-256: `93a6ba37b1098ee44391f88f8b34197281b6de227fb8ce4251ff83139ef0ce07`. Its native state includes ordinal 1, one settled response and a pending compacted response, plus turn coverage, a 2,004-byte offset and the actual source prefix hash. The two append fixtures confirm the pending response once and suppress the settled response's late token count. Warm rewrite/reload preserves the entire state.

`codex-parser18/producer.patch` adds only a synthetic export test to that upstream revision. To reproduce, copy the three JSONL inputs into `crates/tokscale-core/tests/fixtures/codex-v10-parser18-producer/`, concatenate them in prefix / append-pending / append-settled order to `complete.jsonl`, apply the producer patch, and run `TOKSCALE_CODEX_FIXTURE_OUT=/tmp/fixture cargo test --locked -p tokscale-core --lib message_cache::tests::export_released_codex_v10_parser18_fixture -- --ignored --exact`. The source basename must remain `codex-v10-parser18.jsonl`. The original producer passed twice and generated identical bytes; do not regenerate this legacy fixture from the consumer branch's types.

`codex-v10-parser19.bin` was exported the same way at upstream `aed9e7e1c9d4dbf06ecda786537cf3c2633d8771` (the parser 18 -> 19 OpenCodex combo-attribution bump), using the identical three JSONL inputs from `codex-parser18/`. SHA-256: `da118ed709a4af10387efe1cc9f9f7bd67d852d45cfd1d8a8099e273574fece0`. Its incremental state is byte-identical to `codex-parser18/expected-prefix-state.json`, because the 18 -> 19 bump changed post-parse attribution, not the parser. `codex-parser18/producer-parser19.patch` is the producer test used at that revision; `codex-v10-parser18.bin` now verifies version rejection before payload decoding, like parser 14.

`claude-v12-parser2.bin` was written twice with the unmodified native parser, checkpoint types and writer at upstream `68a4324ab15d4337e295a36e3dff5d4431a182b3`; both runs produced identical 788-byte output. SHA-256: `239285d16f003aabcc5993fa73626e6421a1e46b346212fe1ec625202ed4973b`. It contains two live responses, one retained-only historical response and a populated checkpoint: pending human turn, provider confidence, split-reporting deduplication key and an unclamped 500-token one-hour cache-write bucket. The old checkpoint is deliberately discarded during migration because the billing-aware message digest and conflict state changed, while every message and retention marker survives. The first successful scan rebuilds billing identity and a current checkpoint from live bytes; absent historical responses remain available with unknown billing identity.

To reproduce, check out that exact upstream revision, apply `claude-parser2/producer.patch`, copy its four JSONL inputs into `crates/tokscale-core/tests/fixtures/claude-v12-producer/`, and run `TOKSCALE_CLAUDE_FIXTURE_OUT=/tmp/fixture cargo test --locked -p tokscale-core --lib message_cache::tests::export_released_claude_v12_checkpoint_fixture -- --ignored --exact`. The source path suffix must remain `.claude/projects/synthetic-project/claude-v12.jsonl`. The export test checks native readback, checkpoint integrity, append/fresh equality, and retained history before writing the fixture. The expected JSON files use the upstream message schema; consumer tests check new billing fields separately.
